facts.fact_text: A demonstration was planned to be held on 31 July 2010 in Baku.
A demonstration was planned to be held on 2 April 2011 in Baku.
A demonstration was planned to be held on 17 April 2011 in Baku.
The organisers decided to hold the demonstrations in the centre of Baku, notwithstanding the Baku City Executive Authority's refusals to authorise the proposed locations.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
Each applicant attended one of the demonstrations (as specified in the appendix).
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 31 July 2010 at the places indicated by the organisers.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 at the places indicated by the organisers.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 17 April 2011 at the places indicated by the organisers.
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse them.
According to the official records, all the applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations.
The respective first-instance courts convicted the applicants under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO).
The respective first-instance courts sentenced the applicants to periods of administrative detention ranging from seven to fifteen days, as specified in the Appendix.

The administrative offence reports stated that by deliberately failing to comply with lawful police orders, the applicants had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO).

A summary of other relevant provisions concerning administrative proceedings, the relevant provisions concerning the organisation and holding of public assemblies, and the relevant extracts of international documents can be found in the judgment in the case of Gafgaz Mammadov v. Azerbaijan (no. 60259/11, paragraphs 27-42, 15 October 2015).
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the squares in one of which the organisers proposed to hold the 31 July 2010 assembly were designated for public leisure.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the other places proposed by the organisers for the 31 July 2010 demonstration were areas with heavy traffic.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the places proposed by the organisers for the 2 April 2011 and 17 April 2011 demonstrations were areas with heavy traffic.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 31 July 2010 at the places indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) proposed three alternative locations on the outskirts of Baku for the 31 July 2010 demonstration: a stadium in the Binagadi District, a square in the proximity of Zigh road in the Khatai District, and a yard of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail District.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 at the places indicated by the organisers.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 17 April 2011 at the places indicated by the organisers.

For both the 2 April 2011 and 17 April 2011 demonstrations, the Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) proposed a different location on the outskirts of Baku, namely the yard of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail District.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse them.
The respective first-instance courts convicted the applicants under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO).
The respective first-instance courts sentenced the applicants to periods of administrative detention ranging from seven to fifteen days, as specified in the Appendix.
